title: Domain of a Function Mixing a Radical and a Denominator
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain of y=sqrt(x)/(x-1), combining the restrictions from the numerator's square root and the denominator.

steps.title: Restrict the Square Root
steps.explanation: The numerator sqrt(x) is real only for nonnegative x.
steps.why: Even roots demand a nonnegative radicand.

steps.title: Restrict the Denominator
steps.explanation: The fraction is undefined at the single point x=1.
steps.why: Division by zero is never allowed.

steps.title: Combine Both Conditions
steps.explanation: The domain must satisfy the radical and denominator conditions simultaneously, keeping x >= 0 but deleting x = 1.
steps.why: A natural domain is the intersection of all individual restriction sets.

steps.title: Express as Intervals
steps.explanation: Removing 1 from the half-line [0, infinity) splits it into two intervals; 0 stays included.
steps.why: The puncture at 1 is open, while the endpoint 0 is legal since sqrt(0)/(0-1)=0.
